findings.what: The filename fallback at lines 135-140 still trusts raw record ok truthiness: `if (!r.ok) return false`, then matches `sprint_id`, `step`, and `role` without `isVerifiedLivenessRecord`.
findings.why: A forged unsigned record such as `{ok:true,sprint_id:'SP-X',step:'design',role:'design-lead'}` suppresses an epsilon-stalled finding when the evidence filename matches. I reproduced `evaluate()` returning `ok:true` with `WARPOS_LIVENESS_REQUIRE_SIG=1` and no `attest_sig`.

findings.what: The guard's `OK_PREDICATE` only matches `.ok === true` and `.ok !== true`; it misses equivalent same-session liveness gates like `if (!r.ok) return false`.
findings.why: This is not a hypothetical AST/dataflow objection: the live tree has exactly this missed unverified reader in `epsilon-liveness.js`. A bite-test new reader that reads `dispatch-completions.jsonl` and gates via `!r.ok` produced zero guard violations, so the recurrence-stopper does not actually catch new unverified same-session readers.

findings.what: `SIGNED_FIELDS` does not bind several selector fields that converted readers trust after signature verification, including `run_id`, `phase_id`, `plan_item_id`, `skill`, `sprint`, and `step`.
findings.why: A valid signed record can be copied or edited into another trusted context without invalidating `verifyRecord`. I reproduced `coverage-gate.evaluate()` accepting a record signed for `old-run` after mutating unsigned `run_id` to `target-run`. Similar unsigned selectors are used by `skills-test.js` (`skill`) and `sprint/full.js` (`sprint`/`step`).

parsed.summary: Same-session reader consolidation is not complete. The reviewed `liveness-verified:` pragmas are genuine shape-only/non-ledger or reject-only cases, but there is still an unverified live reader, the guard misses that predicate class, and signature verification does not bind all fields the converted readers use for liveness correlation.
